title: Top players and rank
hints: Your dict from Stage 1 already knows exactly who is on the board: its keys. Both queries are computed from `self.scores` at call time.
To order by score high-to-low and then name low-to-high, sort with a tuple key that negates the score: `key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0])`.
`top` is `sorted(self.scores.items(), key=...)[:k]`, then format each pair with an f-string: `f"{player}({score})"`. Slicing past the end is safe.

For `rank`, don't sort at all: return `1 + sum(1 for s in self.scores.values() if s > mine)`. Ties automatically share the better rank. Check membership first and return `None` if the player is missing.
